questions.explanation: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so P₂ = (5 × 8)/1 = 40 atm.

questions.prompt: A heat engine takes 1000 J from the hot reservoir and rejects 800 J to the cold reservoir in each cycle. What is the efficiency?
In W = PΔV the symbol ΔV stands for the final volume ______ the initial volume.
questions.explanation: ΔV = V_final − V_initial.

questions.prompt: A gas absorbs 1000 J of heat and does 500 J of work. What is the change in internal energy?
In the first law, W is positive when the work is done ______ the system.
questions.explanation: W is the work done by the gas on its surroundings.

questions.prompt: For a heat engine to do work both a hot and a ______ reservoir are required.
questions.explanation: Heat can flow, and work can be extracted, only with a temperature difference.

questions.prompt: The work done by a gas at constant pressure is W = ______.
questions.explanation: Pressure times change in volume.

questions.prompt: The dimensions of the Boltzmann constant are ______.
questions.explanation: k has the unit J K⁻¹, so its dimensions are ML²T⁻²K⁻¹.

questions.prompt: A Carnot engine works between a source at 500 K and a sink at 250 K. What is the efficiency?

questions.explanation: W = PΔV = 200 kPa × (0.11 − 0.1) m³ = 2 kJ (positive, work done by the gas).

questions.prompt: A fixed mass of gas occupies 10 L at 5 atm. It is allowed to expand isothermally to 1 atm. What is the final volume?
questions.explanation: Boyle's law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so V₂ = (5 × 10)/1 = 50 L.

questions.prompt: Charles's law can be written as V₁/T₁ = ______.
questions.explanation: V/T is constant at constant pressure.

questions.prompt: An ideal gas expands isothermally and absorbs 200 J of heat. What is the work done by the gas?
questions.explanation: Temperature is constant, so ΔU = 0 and W = Q = 200 J.

questions.prompt: Like gravitational potential energy, it is the ______ in internal energy that matters, not its absolute value.
questions.explanation: Only the change ΔU = U2 − U1 can be measured and used.

questions.prompt: If the temperature of a system rises, the change in internal energy ΔU is ______.
questions.explanation: U2 > U1 when T rises, so ΔU is positive.

questions.prompt: The ideal gas equation is PV = ______.
questions.explanation: PV = nRT with T in kelvin.

questions.prompt: A heat engine takes 500 J from the hot reservoir and rejects 200 J to the cold reservoir in each cycle. What is the work done per cycle?
In the adiabatic compression step the temperature of the gas rises from T₂ to ______.
questions.explanation: The gas returns to its initial state.

questions.prompt: The unit of the Boltzmann constant is the same as the unit of ______.
questions.explanation: Both are measured in J K⁻¹.

questions.prompt: In one complete cycle a gas absorbs 400 J of heat and rejects 150 J of heat. What is the net work done by the gas in the cycle?
questions.explanation: Over a cycle ΔU = 0, so W = Q = 400 − 150 = 250 J.

questions.prompt: 200 J of heat is supplied to a gas in a rigid (fixed-volume) container. What is the change in internal energy?
questions.explanation: Volume is constant, so W = 0 and ΔU = Q = 200 J.

questions.prompt: In the adiabatic expansion of the Carnot cycle the temperature falls from T₁ to ______.
questions.explanation: The gas cools to the sink temperature T₂.

questions.prompt: A gas at 6 atm has a volume of 10 L. Its temperature is kept constant while its volume is changed to 6 L. What is the new pressure?
questions.explanation: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so P₂ = (6 × 10)/6 = 10 atm.

questions.prompt: The "arrow of time" is related to the ______ of an isolated system.
questions.explanation: Entropy increases with time, so it tells past from future.

questions.prompt: The universal gas constant R has the value ______.
questions.explanation: R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.

questions.prompt: The absolute temperature of a gas is 473 K. What is the temperature on the Celsius scale (use t = T − 273)?
The absolute temperature of an ideal gas changes from 100 K to 50 K. What is the factor by which the average K.E. of a molecule changes?
questions.explanation: ⟨K.E.⟩ ∝ T, so the factor is 50/100 = 0.5.

questions.prompt: When heat is added to a system, its entropy ______.
questions.explanation: ΔQ is positive, so ΔS is positive.

questions.prompt: An isothermal process must be carried out ______.
questions.explanation: Heat needs time to flow in and keep the temperature constant.

questions.prompt: In PV = nRT the temperature must be in ______.
questions.explanation: All gas laws need absolute temperature.

questions.prompt: A gas of volume 4 L at −23 °C is heated to 127 °C at constant pressure. What is the final volume?
questions.explanation: Charles's law with kelvin: V₂ = V₁T₂/T₁ = 4 × 400/250 = 6.4 L.

questions.prompt: A gas of volume 2 L at −73 °C is heated to 527 °C at constant pressure. What is the final volume?
questions.explanation: Charles's law with kelvin: V₂ = V₁T₂/T₁ = 2 × 800/200 = 8 L.

questions.prompt: The absolute temperature of an ideal gas changes from 100 K to 500 K. What is the factor by which the average K.E. of a molecule changes?
questions.explanation: ⟨K.E.⟩ ∝ T, so the factor is 500/100 = 5.

questions.prompt: Decay of plants and animals is an ______ process.
questions.explanation: It cannot be retraced in the reverse order.

questions.prompt: Gay-Lussac's law applies at constant ______.
questions.explanation: At constant V, P/T = constant.

questions.prompt: The temperature of a gas is 400 °C. What is the temperature on the kelvin scale (use T = t + 273)?
The SI unit of work is the ______.
questions.explanation: W is measured in joule, 1 J = 1 N m.

questions.prompt: The temperatures used in Carnot efficiency must be in ______.
questions.explanation: Using °C gives a wrong ratio.

questions.prompt: A sealed container of gas that can be heated is an example of a ______ system.
questions.explanation: Heat can cross but mass cannot, so it is a closed system.

questions.prompt: A heat engine takes 1200 J from the hot reservoir and rejects 720 J to the cold reservoir in each cycle. What is the work done per cycle?
When a gas is heated at constant volume its pressure rises because the molecules hit the walls ______ and more often.
questions.explanation: Higher average K.E. makes each collision stronger.

questions.prompt: The P–V graph of an isochoric process is a ______ line.
questions.explanation: Volume is fixed, so the line is vertical.

questions.prompt: A process involving friction is ______.
questions.explanation: Friction dissipates energy, so the process cannot be retraced.

questions.prompt: The Boltzmann constant k equals ______.
questions.explanation: k = R/N_A is the gas constant per molecule.

questions.prompt: Pumping air into a tyre warms the pump because work done on the air raises its ______ energy.
questions.explanation: The work compresses the air and increases its internal energy.

questions.prompt: In an adiabatic compression the temperature of the gas ______.
questions.explanation: Work done on the gas raises its internal energy.

questions.prompt: The SI unit of heat is the ______.
questions.explanation: Heat is a form of energy, so its SI unit is the joule (J).

questions.prompt: The efficiency of a Carnot engine depends only on the ______ of the reservoirs.
questions.explanation: It is independent of the working substance.

questions.prompt: The first law of thermodynamics is written as Q = ______.
questions.explanation: Heat added = rise in internal energy + work done by the system.

questions.prompt: In terms of the number of molecules N, the ideal gas equation is PV = ______.
questions.explanation: With n = N/N_A and k = R/N_A, PV = NkT.

questions.prompt: When ice melts at 0 °C its internal energy ______ while its temperature stays constant.
questions.explanation: The heat supplied raises the potential energy of the particles.

questions.prompt: A fixed mass of gas occupies 5 L at 3 atm. It is compressed isothermally to 10 atm. What is the final volume?
questions.explanation: Boyle's law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so V₂ = (3 × 5)/10 = 1.5 L.

questions.prompt: An ideal gas expands isothermally and absorbs 1550 J of heat. What is the work done by the gas?
questions.explanation: Temperature is constant, so ΔU = 0 and W = Q = 1550 J.

questions.prompt: Internal energy is a function of ______, so its change does not depend on the path.
questions.explanation: ΔU depends only on the initial and final states.

questions.prompt: A pressure cooker is an example of an ______ process.
questions.explanation: The closed container has a fixed volume.

questions.prompt: A fixed mass of gas occupies 9 L at 6 atm. It is allowed to expand isothermally to 1 atm. What is the final volume?
questions.explanation: Boyle's law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so V₂ = (6 × 9)/1 = 54 L.

questions.prompt: The unit of entropy is ______.
questions.explanation: The change in entropy is heat divided by temperature.

questions.prompt: The work done by a heat engine in a cycle is W = ______.
questions.explanation: Heat absorbed minus heat rejected.

questions.prompt: The collisions between the molecules of an ideal gas are perfectly ______.
questions.explanation: No energy is lost in an ideal gas collision.

questions.prompt: Two systems are in thermal equilibrium when they are at the same ______.
questions.explanation: Equal temperature is the only condition for thermal equilibrium.

questions.prompt: For the same mass and temperature, the substance with the greatest internal energy is the ______.
questions.explanation: Melting and boiling need energy that adds potential energy, so the gas has the most.

questions.prompt: Everything outside the system is called the ______.
questions.explanation: Surroundings are the part of the universe outside the system boundary.

questions.prompt: A heat engine takes 500 J from the hot reservoir and rejects 375 J to the cold reservoir in each cycle. What is the work done per cycle?
The coefficient of performance (cooling) of a refrigerator is CP = ______.
questions.explanation: Heat removed from the cold space per unit work.

questions.prompt: A gas of volume 4 L at 47 °C is heated to 127 °C at constant pressure. What is the final volume?
questions.explanation: Charles's law with kelvin: V₂ = V₁T₂/T₁ = 4 × 400/320 = 5 L.

questions.prompt: A fixed mass of gas occupies 5 L at 8 atm. It is allowed to expand isothermally to 5 atm. What is the final volume?
questions.explanation: Boyle's law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so V₂ = (8 × 5)/5 = 8 L.

questions.prompt: A refrigerator removes 600 J of heat from its inside while the compressor does 150 J of work. What is the heat rejected to the room?
A gas in a rigid vessel is at 6 atm and 27 °C. It is heated to 527 °C. What is the final pressure?
questions.explanation: Volume is constant: P₂ = P₁T₂/T₁ = 6 × 800/300 = 16 atm (T in kelvin).

questions.prompt: In the isothermal expansion of the Carnot cycle the gas ______ heat from the hot reservoir.
questions.explanation: Heat Q₁ enters the gas.

questions.prompt: In the word "isobaric", "baros" means ______.
questions.explanation: Greek: iso = same, baros = pressure.

questions.prompt: A heat engine takes 2400 J from the hot reservoir and rejects 1200 J to the cold reservoir in each cycle. What is the efficiency?
A heat engine takes 1000 J from the hot reservoir and rejects 700 J to the cold reservoir in each cycle. What is the efficiency?
When heat is removed from a system, Q is ______.
questions.explanation: Heat leaving the system is negative.

questions.prompt: A Carnot engine works between a source at 600 K and a sink at 320 K. What is the efficiency?
Gay-Lussac's law is also called ______ law.
questions.explanation: P ∝ T at constant volume is Amontons's law.

questions.prompt: An increase in entropy means ______ of energy.
questions.explanation: Part of the energy becomes unavailable for work.

questions.prompt: If the temperature of an ideal gas stays constant, the change in internal energy is ______.
questions.explanation: U depends only on T for an ideal gas, so ΔU = 0.

questions.prompt: A gas absorbs 1200 J of heat and does 500 J of work. What is the change in internal energy?
Air that rises in the atmosphere expands and ______.
questions.explanation: Adiabatic expansion lowers the temperature.

questions.prompt: A gas absorbs 500 J of heat and does 50 J of work. What is the change in internal energy?
The density of an ideal gas of molar mass M is ρ = ______.
questions.explanation: From PV = (m/M)RT we get ρ = m/V = PM/RT.

questions.prompt: For reversible processes the total entropy change is ______.
questions.explanation: Entropy stays constant for reversible processes.

questions.prompt: The curve of an isochoric process is called an ______.
questions.explanation: A vertical line on the P–V graph.

questions.prompt: A heat engine takes 1000 J from the hot reservoir and rejects 600 J to the cold reservoir in each cycle. What is the work done per cycle?
Heat is the energy associated with the kinetic energies of ______ the molecules in a substance.
questions.explanation: Heat counts all the molecules, so a bigger body holds more heat at the same temperature.

questions.prompt: In a reversible process, if heat is absorbed in the direct process, it is ______ in the reverse process.
questions.explanation: Heat flow and work reverse their directions.

questions.prompt: The two ways of raising the internal energy of a system are heating it and doing ______ on it.
questions.explanation: Both heat and mechanical work can increase internal energy.

questions.prompt: A Carnot engine works between a source at 1200 K and a sink at 450 K. What is the efficiency?

questions.explanation: η = 1 only if T₂ = 0 K, which cannot be reached.

questions.prompt: The absolute temperature of an ideal gas changes from 250 K to 1000 K. What is the factor by which the average K.E. of a molecule changes?
questions.explanation: ⟨K.E.⟩ ∝ T, so the factor is 1000/250 = 4.

questions.prompt: A gas in a rigid vessel is at 6 atm and 127 °C. It is cooled to −173 °C. What is the final pressure?
questions.explanation: Volume is constant: P₂ = P₁T₂/T₁ = 6 × 100/400 = 1.5 atm (T in kelvin).

questions.prompt: In one complete cycle a gas absorbs 800 J of heat and rejects 200 J of heat. What is the net work done by the gas in the cycle?

questions.prompt: An ideal gas is assumed to have particles of ______ volume.
questions.explanation: Ideal gas particles are treated as points with negligible volume.

questions.prompt: A refrigerator needs work because heat does not flow from cold to hot ______.
questions.explanation: This is Clausius's statement.

questions.prompt: An ideal gas expands isothermally and absorbs 1400 J of heat. What is the work done by the gas?
questions.explanation: Temperature is constant, so ΔU = 0 and W = Q = 1400 J.

questions.prompt: If heat is removed from a gas at constant volume, both its temperature and pressure ______.

questions.prompt: A gas absorbs 400 J of heat and does 200 J of work. What is the change in internal energy?

questions.explanation: Waste heat warms the environment.

questions.prompt: The P–V graph of an isobaric process is a ______ line.
questions.explanation: Pressure is fixed, so the line is horizontal.

questions.prompt: 1700 J of heat is supplied to a gas in a rigid (fixed-volume) container. What is the change in internal energy?

A heat engine takes 800 J from the hot reservoir and rejects 720 J to the cold reservoir in each cycle. What is the efficiency?
Kinetic theory relates temperature and pressure of a gas to the ______ of its molecules.
questions.explanation: The kinetic theory explains macroscopic properties through molecular motion.

questions.prompt: A gas of volume 20 L at 127 °C is cooled to 47 °C at constant pressure. What is the final volume?
questions.explanation: Charles's law with kelvin: V₂ = V₁T₂/T₁ = 20 × 320/400 = 16 L.

questions.prompt: A refrigerator removes 800 J of heat from its inside while the compressor does 250 J of work. What is the heat rejected to the room?
A gas in a rigid vessel is at 4 atm and −73 °C. It is heated to 227 °C. What is the final pressure?
questions.explanation: Volume is constant: P₂ = P₁T₂/T₁ = 4 × 500/200 = 10 atm (T in kelvin).

questions.prompt: The first stroke of a four-stroke petrol engine is the ______ stroke.
questions.explanation: Intake, compression, power, exhaust.

questions.prompt: At the same temperature and pressure, one mole of any ideal gas contains N_A molecules; N_A is called the ______ number.
questions.explanation: N_A = 6.022 × 10²³ per mole.

questions.prompt: According to Charles's law, volume is directly proportional to the ______ temperature.
questions.explanation: V ∝ T with T in kelvin.

questions.prompt: The efficiency of a heat engine can also be written η = 1 − ______.
questions.explanation: η = (Q₁ − Q₂)/Q₁ = 1 − Q₂/Q₁.

questions.prompt: A device that converts heat energy into mechanical work is a ______.
questions.explanation: A heat engine turns heat into work.

questions.prompt: Melting of ice at 0 °C is an example of an ______ process.
questions.explanation: The temperature stays at 0 °C during melting.

questions.prompt: In an isochoric process the ______ of the system stays constant.
questions.explanation: Isochoric means constant volume.
